extra.message: User-controlled 'host' query parameter is concatenated directly into a shell command string passed to os.system(), allowing arbitrary command execution via shell metacharacters (e.g., host=127.0.0.1; cat /etc/passwd).

User-controlled 'fragment' query parameter is concatenated directly into a Jinja2 Template string, allowing Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI). An attacker can execute arbitrary Python code by injecting Jinja2 expressions like '{{ config }}' or '{{ self.__init__.__globals__.__builtins__.__import__("os").system("id") }}'.

lxml XMLParser is configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False, allowing XML External Entity (XXE) attacks. An attacker can read local files or perform SSRF by sending XML with external entity declarations.

User-controlled 'packet_ref' query parameter is used as a path component joined to a base directory without sanitization, allowing path traversal via '../' sequences to write files outside the intended 'incoming' directory.

User-controlled 'name' query parameter is used as a path component joined to BASE_EXPORT_DIR without sanitization, allowing path traversal via '../' sequences to write files to arbitrary locations on the filesystem.

The password reset endpoint accepts a 'token' parameter but never validates it (comment says 'In production, verify token'). An attacker can reset any user's password knowing only their email address, bypassing authentication entirely.

Uploaded attachments directory is mounted as public static files at /uploads without any authentication or authorization checks. Any unauthenticated user can directly access all uploaded files (potentially sensitive support attachments) by guessing or enumerating filenames.

User-controlled 'card' query parameter is rendered with the Jinja2 '|safe' filter, which disables HTML auto-escaping. Returning the result as HTMLResponse allows reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks.

User-controlled 'lane' query parameter is passed directly to RedirectResponse without URL validation. An attacker can redirect users to arbitrary external sites (e.g., lane=//evil.com) for phishing attacks.

The request body and Authorization header are logged at WARNING level using logger.warning(), which can expose bearer tokens and sensitive request data in plaintext log files, leading to credential leakage.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: User-controlled JSON payload is merged directly into a security-sensitive 'workset' dict via dict.update(). An attacker can override fields like 'role', 'approved', and 'balance' to escalate privileges (e.g., set 'role' to 'admin' or 'approved' to true).

JWT SECRET_KEY has a hardcoded default value 'change-me-in-production-local-dev-only'. If the SECRET_KEY environment variable is not set in production, attackers can forge valid JWT tokens and impersonate any user, including admins.

Hardcoded demo password 'demo123' is used for all seed data users (admin, agents, team leads, and 30 customer users). If seeding runs in production or the password isn't changed, all accounts are trivially compromised.

CSV customer import creates users with a hardcoded default password 'changeme123'. All imported customer accounts share the same well-known password, enabling mass account takeover if the import endpoint is accessible.
SSL certificate verification is explicitly disabled using ssl._create_unverified_context() when making HTTPS requests, making the application vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks.
